findings.reason: the plan's diagnosis is stale against its own base, so the node's fix path and its write paths both change: it must start from the existing join and establish why it does not fire for the three cited instances rather than from a blank "where is the drop" question.
findings.text: s35's leading candidate is "a launch from the queue that leaves the dispatch sidecar naming no run, so the delivery cannot be filed under a review run", yet `join_admitted_plan_review` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:465) does precisely that join — its docstring states the defect verbatim ("Nothing in that launch writes the id back, so promotion's join finds no run and the delivered report is never stored") — it was committed on 2026-10-14 as 02adfe851, an ancestor of the base head bc73d2e1c, and it is reached from the admission pass at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1260 through `_join_admitted_plan_review`; the section names none of these three sites, so a node sent to "establish where the drop lies upstream of the code" will re-derive a diagnosis the tree already records and, following the write path "the modules within reckon/crew/ that the manifest's finding of the cause names", will land in reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py or reckon/crew/queue_admission.py — neither of them granted — and implement a second join beside a working one, which the dispatch contract forbids when the behaviour is already correct

findings.reason: the node writes the gate the bullet names, so naming the wrong condition as the refusal is exactly the choice the section has to settle before dispatch.
findings.text: s36's deliverable judges a plan review "by whether its report parses into the plan-review store", while the second done-when bullet refuses one "whose report carries no RUBRIC or FINDING lines", and these are not the same condition: an empty but well-formed report parses into the store and is still no review, and the promotion-check site s6/§23 already store such a report, so a node cannot tell from the section which of the two a refusal must test and may implement the weaker one

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the sidecar s35 cites at .../plan-review/a-limit-reset-reaches-every-session/r-20261021T143300022479-.../plan-review.json resolves and carries plan_version: 0 with no store_error key; _store_deliveries (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2219), names_a_review_subject (reckon/crew/review.py:2019), _index_append (reckon/ledger.py:2484), _resolve_promotion_outcome (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1411) and review_delivery_refusal (reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:482) all resolve, and the committed ledger row for the run s36 cites does carry role review and a review-of- node id.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s36's second bullet names a different refusal condition from the sentence that governs it, so the store-refusal case and the parse condition a node must implement are two different things.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both nodes put gate logs and arms under the run directory and the run's own scratch tree, both durable under ~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/, with no node-local /tmp path named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new field name plan_review_store and the node ids are mechanism names; no plan label, stage name or ticket number is carried into a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s35's leading candidate is a launch from the queue that leaves the dispatch sidecar naming no run, but that exact join already exists at base and is reached from the production admission pass, and the plan never names it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s35 carries one goal with two clauses ("stored, or says it was not"), the repair and the receipt field being the two halves of the same section title; s36 carries one, the default outcome for a plan review.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s35 and s36 declare no depends-on, informs or gates of their own and neither needs one: s35 lands the store path and the receipt field, s36 the plan-review default outcome, and s36's own bullet 4 keeps the run-review refusal intact, so neither node's done-when requires the other's change.
